data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.AlArrancar
data.value: Check for new versions at startup (at most once a day)

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.AlArrancar.Accesible
data.value: Check for new versions at startup

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.Aplazada
data.value: Installation postponed. The installer has already been downloaded.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.Confirmar.Texto
data.value:
Cuaderno NODISLA will close and the installer for version {0} will open.
Your QSOs and settings are not touched. If you are transmitting or in the middle of a QSO, cancel and finish first.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.Explicacion
data.value: The public releases page on GitHub is checked, without any account or data of yours. If there is a new version, a notice appears at the top; nothing is downloaded or installed unless you ask for it.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.NoAbreNavegador
data.value: Could not open the browser. The page is {0}

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.NoMontado
data.value: Version notifications are not available in this session.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.SinInstalador
data.value: This version has no verifiable installer. Download it from the GitHub page.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.SinNotas
data.value: This version has no release notes.

data.name: Ajustes.Actualizaciones.TituloDelAviso
data.value: A new version of Cuaderno NODISLA is available: {0} (you have {1}).

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.BrilloAyuda
data.value: Raises or lowers black: higher shows some noise; lower makes it fully black.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.ClicParaSintonizar
data.value: Click to tune and wheel to move the VFO

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.ClicParaSintonizarAyuda
data.value: Always goes to the active VFO and never while transmitting. With Shift, fine step (one tenth).

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.ContrasteAyuda
data.value: Radio scale units between black and the brightest colour. Lower: weak signals stand out more.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.DesplazarAyuda
data.value: In CENTER, moving the VFO shifts what is already drawn with the frequency: each signal stays in place instead of smearing diagonally.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.Explicacion
data.value: The spectrum and waterfall sent by the radio itself (FT-710 over its USB port). Choose how it is drawn and what the mouse does over it. None of this changes any radio setting.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.NivelBajoAyuda
data.value: With the automatic floor off, the radio level (0-255) shown as black.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.PasoAyuda
data.value: Multiple the clicked frequency snaps to, and how far each wheel notch moves. Automatic: according to the visible span (500 Hz at 200 kHz, 50 Hz at 20 kHz).

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.PicosAyuda
data.value: The five strongest signals get an amber mark and how far they rise above the noise, in radio scale units.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.SpotsEncimaAyuda
data.value: Callsigns from the cluster list (all nodes, with its filter) at their frequency. Magenta: new entity; green: new band or mode; grey: already worked.

data.name: Ajustes.Analizador.SueloAutomaticoAyuda
data.value: Noise stays dark and signals keep good contrast even when band, preamp or attenuator change, without touching the radio. Remembers each band's floor.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Discrepancia
data.value: Warning: the input “{0}” and the output “{1}” do not seem to belong to the same device. If the radio has a USB codec, both input and output should be marked “RIG”; if they are not, check them before transmitting.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Entrada.Ayuda
data.value: Where the received audio comes from. On the FT-710 it is its USB codec.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Escuchando
data.value: Listening to “{0}”. Speak or tune the radio to a signal to see the level.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Explicacion
data.value: Where the radio's audio comes in and goes out, and who decodes FT8 and FT4.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Muestras.Ayuda
data.value: 48,000 is what the FT-710 codec provides and what FT8 and FT4 expect.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Nivel.Bajo
data.value: {0:0.00} — very low. Raise the codec's recording volume.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Nivel.Satura
data.value: {0:0.00} — CLIPPING. Lower the codec's recording volume in Windows until it stays between 0.20 and 0.60.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.NivelBueno
data.value: The right level is between 0.20 and 0.60. Above 0.90 the codec clips and weak signals are lost; below 0.03 nothing gets through.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.NoMontado
data.value: Audio is not available in this session.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.PreguntarAntes
data.value: Ask before transmitting with the modem

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.PreguntarAntes.Ayuda
data.value: This is what “Don't ask again” turns off. The PTT watchdog, the clock and the output are always required.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.ProbarNivel.Ayuda
data.value: Opens the chosen input and shows the level. It is the only thing on this screen that touches the sound card.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.RecordarPermiso.Ayuda
data.value: The lock on the Digital tab starts open. By default it starts closed in every session.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.RegistrarAlCompletar.Ayuda
data.value: When RR73/RRR/73 is received from the other station, or when your own RR73 goes out after their R+report, the QSO is logged without pressing “Save to log”.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.Salida.Ayuda
data.value: Where the audio is sent to the radio when transmitting.

data.name: Ajustes.Audio.SinModulo
data.value: There is no audio module in this session, so there is nothing to configure here. Close the program and open it again without CUADERNO_SIMULADO.

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.AplicadoVarios
data.value: Saved and applied: {0} nodes, {1} active, logging in as {2}. Unchanged nodes stay connected.

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.Conexion.Ayuda
data.value: Opens or closes the connection to the node

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.IndicativoNoVale
data.value: The call sign “{0}” is not valid: {1}

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.NodoDeEnvioConsejo
data.value: Commands and your own spots (DX …) go only to this node, never to all of them: otherwise they would be repeated across the whole network.

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.Orden.Ayuda
data.value: Command for the node, for example sh/dx

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.PuertoNoVale
data.value: The port of “{0}” is not valid: it must be between 1 and 65535.

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.Simulado
data.value: With simulated ports the cluster is fake, so there is no node to configure. Close the program and open it again without CUADERNO_SIMULADO to choose the node, call sign and password.

data.name: Ajustes.Cluster.SinIndicativo
data.value: There is no call sign to log in with: type it here or create a station profile.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Cifrado.Accesible
data.value: Encryption of the connection to the mail server

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Cifrado.Explicacion
data.value: STARTTLS: port 587 (the usual one). Direct SSL: port 465. None: only for a server on your home network.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.ConexionCorrecta
data.value: Connection OK: the server accepts the account. No e-mail has been sent.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Contrasena.Explicacion
data.value: It is encrypted with your Windows account's data protection and is never shown again.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Explicacion
data.value: The account used to send QSL cards by e-mail. Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, 587, STARTTLS and an app password. Outlook: smtp-mail.outlook.com, 587, STARTTLS.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.NoMontado
data.value: QSL e-mail is not available in this session.

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Probar.Accesible
data.value: Test the connection to the mail server without sending anything

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.TextoDeOmision.Accesible
data.value: Go back to the default subject and body

data.name: Ajustes.Correo.Usuario
data.value: User name (empty if the server does not require authentication)

data.name: Ajustes.Cuenta.ApodoQth.Nota
data.value: Only if you have several QTHs on eQSL.

data.name: Ajustes.Cuenta.RutaTqsl.Nota
data.value: Only if it is not in the usual install location.

data.name: Ajustes.Cuenta.UbicacionTqsl.Nota
data.value: The name you gave the location in TQSL, not your call sign.

data.name: Ajustes.Cuenta.UsuarioVacio
data.value: Empty: the profile call sign is used.

data.name: Ajustes.Cuentas.Explicacion
data.value: One card per service. Passwords are stored encrypted with your Windows account's data protection and are never shown again: the program only says whether they are saved.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Ancho.Ayuda
data.value: Narrower pulls out weaker signals and rejects neighbours better, but struggles above 40 WPM. 100 Hz suits almost everything.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Explicacion
data.value: The cockpit decoder. It listens to the audio input above and never transmits.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Senales.Ayuda
data.value: Besides the main one, reads the other signals in the passband, each on its own line. 1 = main only.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Sensibilidad.Ayuda
data.value: Higher reads weaker signals; lower needs more signal before writing. Noise writes nothing at any setting.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.SinSenal.Ayuda
data.value: In automatic, seconds without the locked signal before searching for another (1 to 60).

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Tono.Ayuda
data.value: Pitch the decoder starts with before it finds a signal.

data.name: Ajustes.Cw.Velocidad.Ayuda
data.value: Speeds that are tracked, from 5 to 60 WPM. Narrowing them avoids mistaking a slow signal for a fast one.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Aplicar.Accesible
data.value: Save and apply the radio settings

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Aplicar.Ayuda
data.value: Saves and switches radio control without closing the log

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Civ.Ayuda
data.value: In hexadecimal (94 for the IC-7300). Empty = the model's factory default.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Descartar.Accesible
data.value: Discard the changes and go back to what was saved

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Detectar
data.value: Detect automatically which port the radio is on

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Detectar.Ayuda
data.value: First tries where it was last time and, if it does not answer, goes through all ports asking ID;

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Detectar.Explicacion
data.value: The radio is recognised by its answer to ID;, never by the port number: there may be other devices on this computer that also talk over serial.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Explicacion
data.value: How the log talks to the radio. While this is set to “None”, the Connect button on the radio panel does nothing.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.GuardadoSinEquipo
data.value: Saved. The log is now without a radio: you type the frequency and mode yourself.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.GuardadoYAplicado
data.value: Saved and applied: {0}{1}. Press Connect on the radio panel to open communication.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.NadaQueProbar
data.value: No radio: there is nothing to test. You type the frequency and mode yourself.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.NoAparece
data.value: The radio was not found on the serial ports. Check that it is on, that the USB cable is connected, that the chosen model is yours and that no other program is holding the port.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.NoContesta
data.value: The connection was opened but the radio does not answer. Check the baud rate (set by the radio's CAT RATE menu).

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.OmniRig.Explicacion
data.value: OmniRig handles two rigs: 1 and 2. The one set here is the one the log follows.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Probar.Accesible
data.value: Test the connection to the radio

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Probar.Ayuda
data.value: Opens the connection, reads identification, frequency and mode, and closes. Does not transmit.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Ptt.Cat.Explicacion
data.value: The radio goes into transmit with the manufacturer's command. This is the normal choice.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Ptt.Dtr.Explicacion
data.value: Same as RTS, but on the other line.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Ptt.Rts.Explicacion
data.value: By raising the serial port's RTS line: audio interfaces with an optocoupler.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Rigctld.Explicacion
data.value: rigctld must already be running. The usual setting is 127.0.0.1 on port 4532.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Simulado
data.value: The program is running with simulated ports, so there is no real radio to configure. Close the program and open it again without CUADERNO_SIMULADO to configure CAT.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.SinProbarConRadio
data.value: Programmed from the manual, not tested with the radio.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.TiempoAgotado
data.value: Timed out ({0:N0} s) looking for the radio. Check that the radio is on and that no other program is holding the port.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Velocidad.Explicacion
data.value: The baud rate is set by the radio, not the cable: it is in its menu, under CAT RATE. The factory default is 38400. If you do not know it, leave automatic detection on: it tries them all.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Via.CatNativo.Explicacion
data.value: Through the radio's serial port. It is the only method that gives filters, noise, contour, meters and memories.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Via.Ninguna.Explicacion
data.value: No radio: you type the frequency and mode by hand.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Via.OmniRig.Explicacion
data.value: For those who already have OmniRig set up with their radio configured.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Via.Rigctld.Explicacion
data.value: For any other radio, or to share the radio with WSJT-X. rigctld must be running.

data.name: Ajustes.Equipo.Vigilante
data.value: The watchdog releases PTT no matter what: when the time runs out, if whatever is transmitting stops giving signs of life, if an error occurs and when the program closes. A stuck PTT burns out the final stage.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Aviso.AltavocesSonSalida
data.value: The chosen speakers are the output to the radio: what you listen to would be transmitted.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Aviso.MicrofonoEsEntrada
data.value: The chosen microphone is the radio's input: what is received would be retransmitted.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Aviso.SalidaNoEsDelEquipo
data.value: The output to the radio is not the radio's codec: your voice would not reach the radio.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Compresor.Ayuda
data.value: Evens out your voice by lowering the peaks. It raises nothing: there is no make-up gain.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.ComprobarFuente
data.value: Check the SSB modulation source via CAT · menu EX

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Escucha.Explicacion
data.value: It only changes what you hear on the PC speakers. The digital modem and the CW decoder get the radio audio untouched.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Explicacion
data.value: The radio is heard through the PC speakers and you talk through the PC microphone using the PTT on the “Phone” panel in Operate. PTT always goes through the watchdog and has a maximum time. On the radio, the SSB modulation source must be set to USB.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Grabacion.Adjuntar
data.value: Attach to the contact when saving

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Grabacion.Adjuntar.Ayuda
data.value: The saved audio is attached to the contact you are typing or editing, and stored with it.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Grabacion.Grabar
data.value: Keep the received audio in memory

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Grabacion.Grabar.Ayuda
data.value: While listening is open, it keeps the last minutes of radio audio in memory. Nothing is written to disk until you press “Save the last”.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Limitador.Ayuda
data.value: No audio burst goes above the ceiling: it protects speakers and ears.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Micro.Explicacion
data.value: Applied to your voice and to recorded messages before they reach the radio. It never raises the level above the input or above the ceiling.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.NoMontada
data.value: Phone through the PC is not available in this session.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Notch.Ayuda
data.value: Finds and removes only steady carriers and whistles. It adds no delay.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.PttConmutado
data.value: Toggle PTT (click to start, click to stop)

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Puerta.Ayuda
data.value: Lowers the background when you are not speaking: fan, keyboard...

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Reductor.Ayuda
data.value: Removes background hiss. Spectral (NR2) removes the most and adds about 11 ms; adaptive (NR1) is gentler and adds no delay.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.SalidaAlEquipo
data.value: Output to the radio (what is transmitted)

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.SoloSeLee
data.value: The menu is only READ; the program changes nothing on the radio. The index comes from the map read from the FT-710 and has not been confirmed against the manual: if the warning does not match what the radio says, correct it here.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Techo.Micro.Ayuda
data.value: The highest level that can go to the radio. It cannot be set above −1 dBFS.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.TeclaDelPtt.Ayuda
data.value: Only while the window is active and never while typing in a text field

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.TeclasDeMensajes.Ayuda
data.value: Only in a voice mode, with the phone panel visible and if the key has a recorded message. Otherwise F1 still opens the help.

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.TiempoMaximo.Accesible
data.value: Maximum phone transmit time in seconds

data.name: Ajustes.Fonia.Titulo
data.value: Phone through the PC (SSB, AM, FM)

data.name: Ajustes.Idioma.Ayuda
data.value: The built-in help is in Spanish. Chapters that have already been translated are shown in your language; the rest are shown in Spanish with a notice.

data.name: Ajustes.Idioma.Explicacion
data.value: The change takes effect immediately, without restarting. The program logs stay in Spanish, and the labels that mimic the radio's front panel (MODE, SPLIT, CLAR…) stay as they are on the radio.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Choques
data.value: Data that did not match between copies

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.ElegirExportar
data.value: Choose where to save the log as ADIF

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.ElegirImportar
data.value: Choose the ADIF file to import

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.ErrorAlExportar
data.value: Could not export: {0} The file has not been written.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Exportar.Accesible
data.value: Export the log to an ADIF file

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Importar.Accesible
data.value: Import an ADIF file into the log

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Parte.NoCuadra
data.value: WARNING: the numbers do not add up; some records cannot be accounted for. Check the file.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Parte.Rescatadas
data.value: {0:N0} confirmations were rescued that would have been lost by discarding the copies.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.Parte.Resumen
data.value: {0}: {1:N0} records read, {2:N0} new, {3:N0} merged ({4:N0} within the file and {5:N0} with the log), {6:N0} already there.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.SinEscritor
data.value: There is no ADIF writer in this session: export is disabled.

data.name: Ajustes.Libro.SinEscritorAlExportar
data.value: There is no ADIF writer in this session: the file has not been written.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.ClubLogApi.Ayuda
data.value: You request it from Club Log support and never share it with anyone.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.ClubLogContrasena.Ayuda
data.value: Your account password, or an application password if you have one.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.EqslContrasena.Ayuda
data.value: The one for your eQSL.cc account.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.HamQthContrasena.Ayuda
data.value: The one for your HamQTH account.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.LotwContrasena.Ayuda
data.value: The one for your ARRL account. It is used to download the confirmations report.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.QrzClaveDeCuaderno.Ayuda
data.value: It is not the account password: QRZ issues it for uploading QSOs.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.QrzContrasena.Ayuda
data.value: For call sign lookups via XML.

data.name: Ajustes.Secreto.TqslFrase.Ayuda
data.value: Only if your certificate has one. Read the notice below before typing it.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.Bloquear
data.value: Do not transmit outside the band plan

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.Bloquear.Ayuda
data.value: The whole channel occupied by the emission is checked (in CW, carrier plus or minus half the filter), not just the carrier.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.ConfirmarLiberar
data.value: You are about to allow transmitting OUTSIDE the band plan on {0}. Do it only if your licence allows it (for example, a special authorisation). The program will stop preventing it on that band.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.Explicacion
data.value: The PTT watchdog applies them to everything that transmits: MOX, tune, modem, phone and CW.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.Liberar.Ayuda
data.value: Allows transmitting outside the plan on this band, for special licences. Asks for confirmation.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.PotenciaMaxima.Ayuda
data.value: The radio's power is lowered to this before transmitting on this band. Empty: no limit.

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.VigilarRoe
data.value: Cut on high SWR or open antenna

data.name: Ajustes.SeguridadTx.VigilarRoe.Ayuda
data.value: Reads the radio's SWR four times a second while transmitting (RM6 and the Hi-SWR alarm on the FT-710; 15 12 on ICOM).

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.AbrirRed
data.value: Also open to the local network (otherwise, this PC only)

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.AbrirRed.Ayuda
data.value: Even when open, only this PC and the listed IPs get in.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.ConfirmarRed
data.value: Other computers on your network will be able to control the radio (and transmit, if allowed). Only the listed IPs will get in. Never open it to the Internet.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.ConfirmarRed.Titulo
data.value: Open the server to the local network?

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.ConfirmarTx
data.value: A connected program will be able to put the radio on the air. The session latch, band plan, SWR, maximum power and time still apply, and every request is logged.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Control
data.value: They may change frequency, mode, VFO, split and power

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Control.Ayuda
data.value: Without this they can only read. Nothing changes while on the air.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.EnviarSpots
data.value: Send the Logbook's spots to TCI clients

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Explicacion
data.value: Other programs (WSJT-X, JTDX, GridTracker, loggers…) can use the radio through the Logbook, which remains its owner. Everything they request goes through the same safeguards as the Logbook.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.IpMala
data.value: These entries are not valid IPs or networks: {0}

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Ips.Ayuda
data.value: Comma-separated. An IP (192.168.1.20) or a network (192.168.1.0/24).

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.PuertoMalo
data.value: Ports must be numbers between 1024 and 65535, and different.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.RecibirSpots
data.value: Show on the bandmap the spots sent by TCI clients

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Rigctld.Ayuda
data.value: For WSJT-X, JTDX, fldigi or GridTracker: radio "Hamlib NET rigctl", address 127.0.0.1:4532.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.SinPeticiones
data.value: No transmit requests in this session.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Tci.Ayuda
data.value: For programs that speak TCI (Expert Electronics): frequency, mode, PTT, power and spots. No audio for now.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Token.Ayuda
data.value: If set, the program must connect to ws://host:port/?token=… Most TCI programs cannot, so it only makes sense with your own programs.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Tx.Ayuda
data.value: Master switch. Off from the factory.

data.name: Ajustes.Servidor.Tx.Nota
data.value: "Allow transmitting in this session" must also be ticked. A program's PTT goes through the band plan, SWR, maximum power, maximum time and PTT owner checks, and is dropped if the program disconnects or stops talking.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.ColaVacia
data.value: Nothing is waiting to be uploaded.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.Completar
data.value: Fill in name, QTH, locator, country, zones… from the QRZ.com (or HamQTH) record

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.Completar.Explicacion
data.value: Only empty fields are filled in: what you type is never overwritten. Without a network or an account the QSO is saved anyway. Without a paid XML subscription, QRZ.com only provides part of the record.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.CuentasEn
data.value: User names and passwords for QRZ.com, HamQTH, LoTW, eQSL and Club Log go in “Accounts & services”.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.CuentasGuardadas
data.value: Accounts saved. They take effect now, without restarting.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.Explicacion
data.value: Every QSO that is saved (form, Digital or net) is uploaded automatically to the ticked services. Without a network it stays in the queue and is retried with increasing waits and at startup. By default, services with credentials are ticked.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.Ficha.Desactivada
data.value: Complete with QRZ.com: turned off in Settings › Uploads & QRZ.

data.name: Ajustes.Subidas.Ficha.Problema
